title: Speier et al. 2017 — A comparison of stimulus types in online classification of the P300 speller using language models
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 10 healthy participants performing a P300 speller task using a 6×6 character matrix. The study compares two stimulus conditions—famous faces and inverted faces—to evaluate their effects on online P300 classification using language models. Data were collected across 2 sessions per subject with 3 runs per session, recorded at 256 Hz from 32 EEG channels using a g.tec amplifier.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired at 256 Hz sampling rate from 32 channels using a g.tec amplifier with left ear reference and AFz ground. Participants performed a P300 row-column speller task with a 6×6 character matrix. Two stimulus conditions were tested: famous face overlays and inverted faces. Stimuli were presented with an inter-stimulus interval of 25 ms and stimulus onset asynchrony of 125 ms. Visual feedback was provided during online classification.
